findings.title: 290-entry path table duplicates the fallback path formula it sits beside
findings.note: All 290 map entries (lines 12-302) follow exactly the same 'data/'+name+'.json' pattern already computed by the fallback at line 8. The transformation is expressed twice: once as code, once as 290 hand-written literals that must stay consistent with it if the path scheme ever changes.

findings.title: Two overlapping HTTP fetch implementations in httpc package
findings.note: Fetch and FetchWithTimeout both implement the same GET-then-handle-response flow; the comment at httpc.go:11 says Fetch is deprecated in favor of FetchWithTimeout, yet main.go:28 still calls the deprecated copy, so both bodies remain live and must be kept in sync.

open_questions.question: Is the paths map generated from an external manifest (e.g. a build step not present in this checkout)? If so this table would be generated/fixture data and out of scope for this family.
Was httpc.Fetch scheduled for removal, and is main.go's continued call to it (line 28) tracked work, or an overlooked migration?

looks_bad_but_fine.why: start/stop/status/legacyHandler are trivial same-shaped stub functions but each represents a distinct command with its own reason to change; not duplication.

not_assessed: Could not check git history for coupled-change frequency between lookup.go's table and its callers; no git log tool was available in this session.
Whether httpc.Fetch is actually still reachable at runtime beyond the single call site in main.go was not traced further (e.g. via reflection or external callers outside this repo).
